abstract.t: This document defines a governance framework for OAuth 2.0 delegation chains that span administrative domains. It specifies how a chain of delegated authorizations is represented, how each link is cryptographically bound to its predecessor and to the domain boundary it crosses, and how governance controls (revocation, scope narrowing, and expiry propagation) are enforced across the entire chain rather than per-link in isolation.

The framework addresses the trust and accountability gaps that arise when an authorization delegated in one domain is exercised in another, enabling verifiable, end-to-end governance of multi-hop delegated access.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: OAuth 2.0 delegation frequently crosses administrative domain boundaries: an enterprise identity provider delegates to a SaaS application, which delegates to an integration partner, which delegates to an automation agent. Each hop is a separately authorized delegation, but the security of the end-to-end access depends on the integrity of the entire chain. This document defines a governance framework for cross-domain delegation chains, binding the links and propagating governance controls across domain boundaries.
This section will describe the cross-domain delegation problem, the limitations of per-link authorization in multi-hop chains, and the motivation for chain-level governance.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals as shown here.

section.name: Chain Representation
section.t: This section will define the structure of a delegation chain: each link carries the delegator's identity, the delegate's identity, the delegated scope, the domain boundary crossed, and a signature binding the link to its predecessor. The chain is represented as an ordered sequence of signed link records, verifiable end-to-end by any party holding the root delegator's public key.

section.name: Domain Boundary Binding
section.t: This section will specify how each link records the domain boundary it crosses and how the domain's trust policy is referenced from the link. A link crossing into a domain MUST carry a reference to that domain's applicable governance policy, so that the receiving domain can verify the delegation complies with its inbound delegation rules.

section.name: Revocation and Scope Narrowing Propagation
section.t: This section will define how governance controls propagate across the chain: when a link is revoked, all downstream links MUST be invalidated; when a scope is narrowed at a link, downstream links MUST NOT exceed the narrowed scope. The section will specify the propagation mechanism (a revocation list or status endpoint scoped to the chain) and the requirements on downstream domains to check propagation status before honoring a delegation.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section will analyze threats to cross-domain chains: link forgery, unauthorized scope expansion across a domain boundary, revocation lag, and complicity of an intermediate domain. For each, the section will identify the mitigation provided by the chain governance framework.
